title: Godot 4 (GDScript) → three.js (TypeScript, browser)
conventions: three.js is a renderer, not a game engine: physics, input mapping, scene files, audio buses and UI are yours to choose. A common stack: three + Rapier (@dimforge/rapier3d-compat) for physics, plain DOM/CSS for UI, Vite for building.

Axes match Godot (right-handed, Y up, cameras look down -Z, meters): positions and quaternions carry over unchanged. Godot's default Euler order is YXZ; set object.rotation.order = 'YXZ' when copying Euler angles.

Godot scenes: export meshes and materials as glTF 2.0 (Scene → Export As → glTF 2.0) and load them with GLTFLoader; recreate the node logic in TypeScript classes that own an Object3D. ReversePort can write a TypeScript scene-builder module from a .tscn (port_scene).
Each GDScript becomes a TypeScript class with update(dt) and fixedUpdate(dt) methods; a small game loop calls them from renderer.setAnimationLoop.
Dispose geometries, materials and textures when removing objects (the browser does not free GPU memory for you).

Checked against three r187: 'three' and 'three/webgpu' both import build/three.core.js, so importing from both does not load two copies of the core. WebGPURenderer, node materials and RenderPipeline come only from 'three/webgpu', TSL from 'three/tsl'; ShaderMaterial and onBeforeCompile do nothing under WebGPURenderer.

Node names from a Godot glTF export can change on load (three r187): GLTFLoader renames a repeated name with a suffix (createUniqueName: 'Wheel', 'Wheel_1') and PropertyBinding.sanitizeNodeName turns spaces into '_' and drops [ ] . : /. Look objects up by the names three shows (getObjectByName), and keep node names unique and plain in the export.

Headless testing, the counterpart of `godot --headless`: Chromium headless with software WebGL 2 (SwiftShader, through Playwright) runs a three.js page in CI. three announces every Scene and renderer to window.__THREE_DEVTOOLS__ ('observe' events), which gives a test the live scene without changing the page. SwiftShader frame times are CPU rendering: compare them before and after, never as real fps; draw calls, triangles and programs (renderer.info) are exact. Headless rAF timestamps stay on the 60 Hz grid even when a frame ran long, so time frames with performance.now().

entries.from: an imported .glb with compression (Godot imports it as-is)
entries.to: GLTFLoader with setDRACOLoader(new DRACOLoader()), setMeshoptDecoder(MeshoptDecoder) or setKTX2Loader(new KTX2Loader().detectSupport(renderer))
entries.notes: Read extensionsUsed in the file: KHR_draco_mesh_compression, EXT_meshopt_compression and KHR_texture_basisu each need their decoder set on the loader or loading fails. In three r187 DRACOLoader and KTX2Loader find their decoders next to themselves (examples/jsm/libs, through import.meta.url), so setDecoderPath is only needed when the files are served elsewhere.

entries.to: an import map with "three/addons/" pointing at the whole examples/jsm folder, or a bundler
entries.notes: Addons import each other by relative path (GLTFLoader imports ../utils/BufferGeometryUtils.js and ../utils/SkeletonUtils.js), so serving single addon files gives a 404 on the next import. Serve or copy whole folders (loaders, utils, libs).

entries.to: '/models/Car.glb' under the dev server's public/ folder, written with the exact capitals
entries.notes: Godot resolves res:// the same on every OS. A web host on Linux is case-sensitive: a path that loads on macOS or Windows can be a 404 after deploy, and the loader then reports the HTML 404 page as a parse error ("Unexpected token '<'").

entries.from: a node mirrored with a negative scale
entries.to: the same negative scale on the Object3D
entries.notes: Works as in Godot: WebGLRenderer flips the front face when the world matrix has a negative determinant, so mirrored meshes still face out.

entries.from: godot --headless --check-only / a scene run in CI
entries.to: the page in headless Chromium (Playwright) with software WebGL 2, console and page errors collected, a screenshot judged for blank frames
entries.notes: A scene that throws or never renders shows one flat colour: test for that instead of comparing exact pixels across machines; keep screenshot baselines per environment.
